question.text: Options are known as 'wasting assets' because:

answer.text: Their time value gradually falls to zero by expiry date
They always result in a loss for the buyer
The underlying commodity deteriorates in quality
The exchange charges daily holding fees

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, options are called wasting assets because their time value gradually falls to zero by the expiry date, with time decay that is non-linear. The Trap: Options do not always result in losses; the quality of the physical commodity is irrelevant to time decay; no daily exchange holding fees apply. Note: The "wasting" refers specifically to the time-value component of the premium, which erodes as expiry approaches.
